doFirst.why: This is insurance, not a starter. Pitts keeps the tight end slot — see below. You carry five running backs and exactly one tight end, and Mayer is the largest ownership move on either league's wire (+3.02 in a day) at only 27.8% rostered, which is the market catching up to a role that has already changed: Bowers is OUT with a knee and Las Vegas extended Mayer on Friday to start in his place. On the drop: Monangai is rostered in 78.6% of leagues and I am telling you to cut him anyway. He hyperextended his knee on Aug 16, missed roughly a month, practised for the first time on Sept 7, was never cleared, and Swift sits above him on Chicago's depth chart. ESPN lists him ACTIVE at 10.3 — that label is a guess the market has not repriced. Chem's only flex is RB/WR and both McLaurin and Tuten project ahead of him, so he is your RB5 in a slot you cannot use. Act before 17:00Z: Mayer's game is at 20:25, but Chicago kicks at 17:00 and a locked Monangai cannot be dropped.

trades.headline: Teca carry exactly one quarterback. Stafford outprojects Drake Maye and is worth +0.9 a week to them, before the bye they have no answer for.
trades.yourSurplus: Josh Allen is your QB1 every week of the season. Stafford has never started for you and this week returned 4.1 points from a Thursday game you had no reason to watch. The seat returns nothing.
trades.theirHole: Drake Maye is the only quarterback on their roster. One bad Sunday, one injury, or the New England bye and their QB slot is empty.
trades.yourLineup: Odunze becomes your fourth receiver behind Jefferson, Garrett Wilson and McLaurin, and a real body for the Achane and Warren byes. Your flex does not change this week.
trades.theirLineup: Stafford (17.6) starts over Maye (16.4) for +1.2 at quarterback; DK Metcalf (12.2) fills Odunze's flex seat for -0.3. Net +0.9. They are six receivers deep, so Odunze is the one they can lose without touching their top two.
trades.risk: Called LONGSHOT for a reason: nobody trades a starting receiver for a quarterback who has already played his week, so do not send this today — propose it once this slate is over and Stafford is next week's asset again. Odunze is also QUESTIONABLE with a calf and is a genuine game-time call. And be honest about the shape of it: the one-week gain to you is +0.2. The case is season-long — a quarterback who will never start for you becoming a receiver who might — and season-long value is the one thing this brief cannot price, because only weekly projections are published.

candidates.note: Mark Andrews looks like the league's biggest blunder and is not one. He is rostered in 83.3% of leagues and free here, which is exactly the shape of a real error — but the market is slow to demote a name, and ESPN's 10.1 is well above the consensus, which has him around TE16 for Week 1. The sources genuinely split: PFN's Week 1 piece says start him now and sell high, on the grounds that Likely's departure opens snaps and Indianapolis allowed the third-most red-zone trips last season; SI says fade him, on no season above 55 catches since 2022, yards-after-catch collapsing to 23.9% of his receiving yards in 2025, and a run-heavy script against the Colts. Side with the fade for this week: a touchdown-dependent tight end in a run-heavy game is a coin flip, and Pitts has the better matchup by a distance. Worth holding in mind for the Pitts bye, not worth a roster spot today.

Jakobi Meyers is rostered in 79.4% of leagues and is a free agent here — the most valuable thing a wire can hold. He is the steady-volume receiver in a Jacksonville offence that is heavily favoured, and he is the slot starter on the Jaguars' official Week 1 depth chart rather than a projection guess. He does not crack your lineup behind Jefferson, Garrett Wilson and McLaurin, so there is nothing urgent here — he is the first name to take if McLaurin's flex seat stops paying, and in Chem a claim costs nothing lasting anyway because priority resets weekly.

Trevor Lawrence is rostered in 88.3% of leagues and is a free agent in Chem. Guillo-tinas dropped him on Friday to add Keenan Allen, which is the kind of mistake that does not usually sit on a wire for long. You do not need a QB2 behind Josh Allen and this is not a move for today — but Allen's bye is Week 7, and Lawrence is the best quarterback anyone in this league can have for nothing.

Ravens D/ST is rostered in 90.2% of leagues and unowned here — the single most widely rostered player on Chem's wire. Not a Week 1 move: your Jaguars project 8.6 against Deshaun Watson's Browns and rank as a top-three streaming defence this week. Note it for the Jacksonville bye in Week 7.
